data.body:
PROVEN RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1, 2026-08-09)

Mechanism: `summary_compute` resolves each requested identifier through `show_state`, but discards the resolved state's `alias` and returns the caller-supplied token as `ticket_id` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:386-411`). The summary schema and CLI/library/MCP contracts likewise omit alias (`src/rebar/schemas/summary.schema.json:5-16`; `src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:205-212`; `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:260-263`). Thus a short prefix remains the most local identifier and is echoed back even after successful resolution: live `rebar summary b68c --output json` returned `ticket_id: b68c` with no alias, while `rebar show b68c` resolved the canonical ticket and exposed alias `anthracite-maize-frog`. The agent then copies the locally salient prefix.

Discriminating proof: pinned `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, temperature 0, single-turn, 5 repeats x 5 tickets. Current guidance plus summaries whose local `ticket_id` values were four-character tokens yielded 25/25 four-character `rebar show` commands and 0/25 aliases, despite an earlier catalog containing every alias. Changing only the local summary to add each alias yielded 25/25 alias commands. Leaving summary unchanged but adding an adjacent affirmative alias rule also yielded 25/25 aliases. Removing only the AGENTS quick-reference `tid["id"]` example had no effect (0/25 aliases, 25/25 full IDs), rejecting example priming as the cause. With alias plus affirmative rule, the identity-sensitive negative control emitted full canonical UUIDs in 25/25 `rebar-ticket:` trailers, proving the intervention does not indiscriminately replace canonical identities.

Resolver alternative rejected: `_ids.py:278-310` resolves aliases and fails closed for ambiguous prefixes. Live 2dce/2e89 summary inputs were rejected as ambiguous, while aliases resolve. Resolver ergonomics is not the defect. `_short_prefix` already computes the shortest currently unique prefix (`src/rebar/_engine_support/lookups.py:46-61`).

Defect legitimacy: incomplete implementation of the approved WS5 agent-fitness intent. Original authority `c5d79b58b6e829b336684c46cfc482c17c111c7a:REMEDIATION_PROPOSAL.md`, WS5e lines 336-344, explicitly requires create to return id+alias so agents need no second show and requires interface parity; current library/MCP comments preserve that rationale (`_lib_writes.py:95-97`, `_mcp_writes.py:57-68`). The compact summary surface drops the agent-facing alias that WS5e made available.

Caller-dependency gate: expected post-fix behavior is additive alias availability/foregrounding on summaries while retaining fail-closed prefix resolution and canonical IDs for identity-sensitive contracts. Serena plus rg found only `summary_cli` and public `rebar.summary` as direct callers; MCP delegates to the library. The schema permits additive properties, contract tests validate shape rather than exact equality, and no caller was found that behaviorally depends on alias absence. No blocker to Phase 2.

Phase 1 stops here; no code/test change, claim, plan review, or ticket transition was performed.
